database_extractor.ordering_model: SEMANTIC for the single-pass line scan and for parameter list order (both reflect source-code order and are relied on for correctness, e.g. a variable's type must be recognized before a later Command/Adapter check on that name); INCIDENTAL for dict-key iteration order within a single line's regex matches.
r6_readiness_missing_characterization: Branch-order interaction tests: no test currently proves what happens when two different operation-detection branches could both match the same physical line (e.g. a line matching both COMMAND_TEXT_RE and EXECUTE_RE patterns), which is exactly the kind of interaction a future extraction into separate detector objects could silently change.
_split_args edge cases (nested parentheses, quoted commas, empty trailing argument) have no direct unit test; _wrapper_parameters and _parameter both depend on it for correctness.
No test isolates variable/type state tracking from operation emission, so a future extraction of the 'variable scope' responsibility has no unit-level safety net independent of full extract() runs.
No test for multiple classes in one file re-using the same variable name with different declared types (would validate that class/method-boundary state resets are complete and correctly scoped).

flow_resolver.monkeypatch_note: tests/test_v1_unittest.py::test_v2_r4_1_path_ids_use_complete_canonical_identity_and_guard_collisions monkeypatches resolver._path_id (an instance-level function attribute reassignment) and resolver._path_identities directly on a live instance to force a deterministic collision. Any future extraction of _path_id/_add_path into a separate collaborator must preserve this exact patch point or update this pre-existing test deliberately in that later round.
flow_resolver.ordering_model: SEMANTIC for _flow_status's fixed status precedence and for path/node identity (which encodes the traversal path itself); DETERMINISTIC_BUT_NOT_SEMANTIC for the final flows/paths list ordering (explicitly re-sorted by id after construction) and for project_sequence (first-seen order); INCIDENTAL for graph_nodes/graph_edges dict insertion order during traversal (also re-sorted before being placed into the output flow dict).
r6_readiness_missing_characterization: The exact _stable_id hashing algorithm (a simple polynomial rolling hash) is not pinned to a specific expected numeric output anywhere -- only cross-run equality/inequality is characterized. A future extraction that changes _stable_id's implementation (even while keeping its signature) would not be caught unless output IDs are also pinned to specific known values for at least one fixture.

No test exercises two entry points in the same resolve() call that share an overlapping call graph, to confirm graph_nodes/graph_edges/paths dicts (created fresh per entry point inside the for-loop) never leak state between entry points within a single call.

_flow_status's full precedence order (truncated_depth > cycle > unresolved_boundary > data_endpoint > dead_end) is only partially exercised in isolation; no single fixture produces both a cycle and a truncated_depth path in the same flow to directly confirm truncated_depth wins.

No characterization of a method that both has direct data_access operations AND calls another method in the same _walk invocation, to confirm both branches execute and both contribute paths (the two loops in _walk are independent but untested together at the unit level).

flow_resolver.state_model_evidence: self._path_identities, self.method_calls, self.unresolved_calls, self.data_by_method, self.proc_by_operation, and self.sql_by_operation are all reassigned at the very top of resolve(), before any use; calling resolve() twice on the same instance with the same inputs produces output identical to a fresh instance (tests/test_v4_1_r5_flow_resolver_characterization.py::RepeatedTraversalAndOrderingTests / StateResetAndReuseTests). main.py never actually reuses one instance for multiple resolve() calls, but the reset guarantees it would be safe if it did.
